nodes.label: Example Heartbeat of Each Class (figure)
nodes.description: 2x4 grid of single segmented ECG beats, one per MIT-BIH class (N, L, R, V, A, F, f, /, IDs 1-8). Amplitude (standardised units) vs sample index at 360 Hz, ~275 samples per beat, dotted vertical line marks the centred R-peak at ~sample 137.

nodes.label: R-peak Centred Beat Window (~275 samples @ 360 Hz)
nodes.rationale: Each beat is segmented as a fixed-length window around the annotated R-peak (~137 samples before/after, ~0.76 s total), aligning QRS complexes so classifiers compare morphology at fixed positions.

nodes.label: MIT-BIH 8 Beat Classes (N, L, R, V, A, F, f, /)
nodes.description: Class IDs 1-8: N normal, L left bundle branch block, R right bundle branch block, V premature ventricular contraction, A atrial premature, F fusion of ventricular and normal, f fusion of paced and normal, / paced.

nodes.label: Class-specific Beat Morphology
nodes.description: Visible differences: N sharp narrow QRS with deep S; L notched/double-peaked wide QRS and broad T; R deep wide S wave; V wide QRS with secondary bump and prolonged negative deflection; A narrow QRS with prior baseline drift and noisy post-QRS; F tall narrow monophasic peak; f very sharp spike (~8) with secondary bump; / wide slow paced complex with deep trough and rising baseline.

nodes.label: Per-beat Amplitude Standardisation
nodes.rationale: Y-axis values in roughly -3..8 range centred near 0 suggest beats are z-scored/normalised during preprocessing; a leading edge artefact (spike at sample 0) appears in several beats, likely from filtering/normalisation at window boundaries.

hyperedges.label: Beat segmentation and normalisation producing class-separable morphologies
